featured_reviews.name: Stanley Vaz
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Avatara, one does not merely dine—one participates in a carefully orchestrated culinary narrative that challenges every preconceived notion of vegetarian cuisine.

From the moment you are seated, the service establishes its quiet authority: attentive without intrusion, polished without pretension. Among the team, Viraj stands out—not with flamboyance, but with a rare, intuitive finesse. His understanding of the menu is not rehearsed, but lived; each course arrives not just as food, but as a story, delivered with precision and warmth.

The cuisine itself is nothing short of revelatory. In a world where vegetarian fare is often relegated to the periphery, Avatara asserts dominance. Every plate is a study in balance—texture, temperature, acidity, and depth all meticulously calibrated. Ingredients are elevated beyond their humble origins, transformed into expressions that are both rooted and avant-garde.

What distinguishes Avatara is its restraint. There is no unnecessary theatrics, no overindulgence in molecular excess. Instead, the kitchen demonstrates confidence—allowing flavours to speak, yet ensuring each bite leaves a lasting impression. It is this quiet mastery that aligns the restaurant with the philosophy of Michelin-starred establishments.

In its totality, Avatara delivers an experience that is immersive, thoughtful, and deeply satisfying. It is not simply one of the finest vegetarian meals—it is one of the finest meals, period.

The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

Tried Shankar Mahadevan’s @malgudi.ind in Chembur during my recent Mumbai trip, a restaurant that’s become quite popular for its modern take on South Indian food. We started with the Anna Style Crispy Lotus Root, which had a tangy tamarind-heavy flavour and worked well as a snack. The much-hyped Mulbagal Dosa, though visually interesting with its parcel-like shape, tasted fairly ordinary. The Davangere Benne Podi Dosa followed a similar route, comforting but not very memorable beyond the podi and butter.

For the main course, we ordered Sanchi’s Vegetable Stew with Appam and Veg Malabar Curry with Malabar Parotta. The curry and parotta were satisfying, but the stew felt too watery and lacked the comforting richness you expect from a good appam-stew combination.

The real standout was the Filter Kaapi Panna Cotta. Smooth, creamy, and packed with coffee and jaggery flavour, it easily ended up being the best thing on the table.

Sambhar replaced by Coconut based gravy in a bowl and button idlys immersed in them, so that they absorb all the flavours of the gravy within them, each bite of every piece of the Idly kept us craving for more! A very great and unique experience for us.

All this ended with a supurb dose of Filter Coffee, customised to our choice of regular or strong and that really left us super satisfied.

There is no parking available here, one has use the Pay and Parking place of the shopping mall just adjesannt to this place.

Overall, a must visit place if we happen to be in this area anytime. One may need to wait for tables, for its being occupied with people who are in no hurry while enjoying the food here!

The parotta was very rubbery and not enjoyable at all. They serve both chicken and mutton saru, but the taste was below average and the spice level was overwhelming. None of the food we ordered stood out in terms of taste.
